label: Higher Distress, Highly Educated Female, Heavy Use
summary: This profile is characterized by comparatively higher loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Respondents in this group also tend to be highly educated and report more than 5 hours of use.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate degree or above, more than 5 hours of use
behavior_markers: Reports more than 5 hours of use

label: Profile 1
summary: Respondents in this profile report comparatively low loneliness, low depressive symptoms, and very low anxiety symptoms.
demographic_anchor: Typically male, educated to graduate level or above, and reporting 1–3 hours in the referenced activity range.
behavior_markers: Low average loneliness on the UCLA-8 indicator
Low average depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9 indicator
Very low average anxiety symptoms on the GAD-7 indicator
Represents a relatively low-distress respondent pattern within the sample

label: Educated women with elevated loneliness but comparatively low depression and anxiety
summary: This profile is characterized by higher reported loneliness alongside comparatively lower depressive and anxiety symptoms. It suggests respondents who feel socially disconnected more often, while not showing similarly elevated levels of broader mood or anxiety distress.
demographic_anchor: Typically female, with graduate-level education or above, and associated with the 1-3 hours category.
behavior_markers: Reports relatively elevated loneliness compared with other symptom dimensions
Shows comparatively low average depressive symptoms
Shows comparatively low average anxiety symptoms
Presents a pattern where social disconnection is more prominent than generalized emotional distress
tone: Socially disconnected but otherwise comparatively emotionally stable
